claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts can oxidize ethanol through a complete 12-electron process.
PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have high selectivity for the complete 12-electron ethanol-oxidation pathway.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are a random, homogeneous solid solution.
Surface-atom heterogeneity in high-entropy alloys produces neighboring sites with different local electronic structures that can tune reaction selectivity.
The random PtPdRhRuIrOs surface has a wide, approximately Gaussian distribution of adsorption energies.
Strong-binding sites stabilize ethanol-derived intermediates needed for C-C bond cleavage.
Weak-binding sites facilitate desorption and further oxidation of reaction fragments.
Complementary strong- and weak-binding sites jointly promote complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
Mild annealing can induce limited local ordering or slight compositional segregation without major phase separation or sintering.
Increasing local ordering narrows the surface adsorption-energy distribution.
Narrowing the adsorption-energy distribution diminishes the ensemble of complementary dual active sites.
The mildly annealed catalyst will have lower activity than the random-alloy baseline.
The mildly annealed catalyst will have lower selectivity for complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation than the random-alloy baseline.
Annealing-induced ordering will increase acetaldehyde or acetate formation relative to CO2 formation.
The proposed mechanism should hold only under conditions that do not induce bulk segregation or particle sintering.
The proposed mechanism is falsified if verified local ordering produces no significant decrease in complete-oxidation selectivity or instead increases it relative to the random-alloy control.
